verdictStatement: Three blockers. The demarcation carriage is genuinely verbatim (every claimed block byte-matches file 02 after markdown-structure folding per freeze section 7.7), the non-interference analysis against the applied TS/Rust authorities is sound where it is stated, all 27 recorded digests reproduce including the prototype pin and its seven files, and the four tensions are honestly reported. But the artifact records a false measurement against the applied TypeScript provider authority (it attributes delivery.v2's RUST substrate transport string and handshakeRequired list to TypeScript major 1), its central exhaustiveness invariant fails on its own bytes (the 'refusal' message maps to no function family), and the hostile-conformance surface cannot exercise half of J-2's own definition of a provider fault. All three repair textually in a v2 successor; none invalidates the descriptor-layout/octet-identity architecture itself.

blockers.class: false recorded measurement against applied authority (freeze 7.2.2 hard-comparison class)
blockers.finding: The cell headed typescriptMajor1 attributes two bindings to the TypeScript major-1 provider that are measurably the RUST substrate's in delivery.v2 (47b6cfd1...4e3cabf3). (a) The quoted transport string 'length-delimited canonical CBOR over inherited stdin/stdout' is $.rustSemanticSubstrate.providerProtocol.transport; the TypeScript binding reads 'bidirectional inherited pipes: length-delimited canonical CBOR on stdin/stdout' ($.typescriptSemanticSubstrate.providerProtocol.transport). (b) 'a handshakeRequired field list of its own (protocolMajor, providerBuildId, rustCommitHash, hostTriple, targetTriple, sysrootDigest, capabilities)' is $.rustSemanticSubstrate.providerProtocol.handshakeRequired verbatim; the TypeScript list is the fourteen-field $.typescriptSemanticSubstrate.identity.handshakeRequired (protocolMajor, providerBuildId, providerDescriptorSha256, runtimeDescriptorSha256, nodeVersion, v8Version, modulesAbi, typescriptVersion, typescriptCompilerSha256, typescriptStdlibMerkleRoot, defaultWorkBudgetProfileId, defaultWorkBudgetProfileSha256, platformId, capabilities). rustCommitHash and sysrootDigest in a TypeScript provider handshake are facially wrong. The artifact's own discipline ('the bound of each measurement is the claim') makes a misattributed measurement a defect of the measured cell, not a typo.
blockers.survives: The design consequence drawn from the cell survives under the correct quotes: 'stdout is protocol-only from process start through EOF...' IS the exact TypeScript substrate text ($.typescriptSemanticSubstrate.providerProtocol.stdout, byte-verified), the TS transport is substantively the same stdin/stdout length-delimited canonical CBOR, and 'a closed host-to-worker frame set that includes Hello and Cancel' is true (closedHostToWorkerFrames[0]='Hello', [6]='Cancel'). Multiplexing foreclosure and the fd3/fd4 design need no structural change; the repair is textual in a successor.
blockers.repairShape: v2 successor re-quotes the TypeScript substrate's own transport and handshakeRequired lines at the same digest.

blockers.class: exhaustiveness invariant fails on the subject's own bytes
blockers.finding: The exhaustiveness clause states 'Every control message belongs to exactly one function family below', and the acceptance framing of this candidate is a closed sixteen-message vocabulary mapped onto the five permitted functions. Measured: the vocabulary has 16 members, the union of functions[].messages has 15, and 'refusal' belongs to NO family (F-1 [], F-2 hello/helloAck/ping/pong/shutdown/shutdownAck, F-3 select/selectAck, F-4 cancel/health/healthReport/resourceReport/fault, F-5 effectRequest/effectResult). By the artifact's own rule, a message outside the family mapping is 'anything else - ... a typed refusal', which is incoherent applied to the refusal message itself. 'refusal' smuggles no sixth capability - it is plausibly F-2 supervision or a declared cross-cutting enforcement message - but the invariant as written is false on the artifact's own table, and the closed envelope is the exact surface DR-102's acceptance cell names.
blockers.repairShape: Assign 'refusal' to a family (or declare it the envelope's single cross-cutting enforcement message, excluded by name from the family rule) in a v2 successor.

blockers.class: acceptance-evidence gap: a J-2 race constituent no CC class exercises
blockers.finding: J-2 defines the provider-plane fault as 'surfaced to the host as a boundary event, e.g. EOF-mid-stream or the owning participant's fault report'. CC-1's closed event set is {cancel-issued, provider-final-octet, control-fault, provider-EOF, process-death, teardown-initiated}: it contains no provider-fault-report event, and no other class supplies one (CC-4 is EOF/death injection; CC-8's fault fixtures are CONTROL-plane fault frames, a different event kind). Every J-2 ordering in which the provider fault is the owning participant's fault report rather than an EOF is therefore unexercised by the specified conformance surface. 'Control fault versus provider fault' is one of the five joins file 02 names, and CC-1..CC-11 are, by the artifact's own words, 'the hostile half's specification' of the acceptance-evidence cell - a named join whose definition is only half reachable by the fixture classes is a gap in that cell, not a harness detail deferrable to DR-G21.
blockers.repairShape: Add provider-fault-report (owning-participant boundary report) to CC-1's event set, or add a dedicated class, in a v2 successor.

advisories.finding: Claims the five-function list, must-not list, races/joins paragraph, and closing rule 'appear here twice each by design'. Measured occurrence counts on the subject bytes: five-function fragments 2 (list plus distribution across F-1..F-5's function fields, each fragment verbatim), must-not list 2, closing rule 3, races/joins paragraph 1. The races/joins paragraph appears once, in demarcationCarriedVerbatim only; the guidance misdescribes the artifact's own structure (MENTIONING-vs-CARRYING class, benign in direction).

'Proves no receiver anywhere compares control frames by bytes or derives identity from them' overclaims: a fixture class driving byte-different serializations demonstrates behavioral indifference on the exercised vectors; it cannot prove the universal negative 'no receiver anywhere'. The operative pass property (identical state transitions, identical merged event order, identical responses) IS testable as stated and suffices; the 'proves' sentence should claim what the fixtures show.

The forward symmetry clause is narrower than the prohibition it mirrors. nonCanonicalByConstruction forbids deriving 'identity, signature, digest, equality-of-record, or any evidence commitment' from control-frame bytes; ID-DEP-7's forward clause names only 'identity, signature, or evidence commitment'. A successor that byte-compares logged control frames (audit-log replay equality, a digest-of-frames log index) is inside the prohibition but outside the forward ride obligation as written. Align the two lists in a successor.

Standings are recorded for six rows (DR-007 HARD-BLOCKED, DR-103/111/112/125 OPEN, DR-118 DECIDED-V1-NOT-INTEGRATED - all six re-verified against the register at digest), but ID-DEP-4 and ID-DEP-6 also ride DR-107, whose live standing is PROPOSED-CLOSED-FOR-REVIEW and is recorded nowhere in the artifact, and DR-G07/DR-G21/DR-105/DR-120 standings are likewise unmeasured. No recorded standing is false; the measured set does not cover every ridden row.

CC-6 exercises 'helloAck proposing a different controlMajor than offered', and handshake step 2 requires helloAck.controlMajor equal the hello's, but no refusal family is assigned to that host-side violation: RF-1 as written covers the component-side unsupported-hello case, RF-3 covers stableId/digest echoes, RF-8 covers replay/re-negotiation. The family for a mismatched helloAck controlMajor is unassigned; the fixture's typed outcome is therefore underdetermined.

The obligation extends to 'any future subprotocol whose framing is carrier-sensitive' and CC-9 requires carrier boundaries preserved for a fixture subprotocol 'declared carrier-frame-sensitive'. fd0/fd1 are POSIX pipes: byte streams with no observable write boundaries, so the declared transport cannot in general provide carrier-boundary preservation. Harmless for both existing majors (length-delimited canonical CBOR is self-delimiting, as the artifact itself notes); the forward clause promises a property the transport cannot carry and should be scoped or dropped in a successor.

Freeze 7.2.2.1 mode (a caveat/justification is a measurement): the absent seq-overflow handling is justified with 'a channel approaching it has long since violated bounds discipline', but no per-channel frame-count bound exists anywhere in the contract - each of 2^53 frames would individually be lawful, so the justification is false. The operative rule (exceeding uint53 is RF-7) stands on its own and needs no false support.

The F-1..F-5 function strings are each verbatim fragments of the five-function list. verifiedClean.nonInterference: delivery.v4's derivedFrom operations touch none of the quoted v2 clauses (no operation mentions transport, stdout, Cancel, or closedHostToWorkerFrames). T-4's composition claim verified against delivery.v2's actual frame-order text: Hello is closedHostToWorkerFrames[0], normalPhases[0] is 'Hello/HelloAck', and delivery.v2 contains no handshake deadline ('timeout'/'deadline' zero occurrences), so a child silent on stdout awaiting a post-selectAck host Hello violates nothing. fd2 claim matches delivery.v2's 'stderr is a non-authoritative diagnostic byte stream'. T-1's supervision-scoped cancel authors no provider semantic frame and is disclosed as pending, not settled; T-2 and T-3 name real bytes (file 04 lines 68-69 and 182 verified). The Rust major-2 claim verified in the v4 overlay's enums: Hello/HelloAck framed, 'stdout-byte' is a typed event-kind with transition and fallback coverage. R-1: the candidate's one-channel-per-child/no-reuse/no-pooling model conflicts with none of r1 v1's LN-01..LN-08 conformance claims and v1.9's whatIsUnchanged moves no design decision; no handshake/negotiation/teardown state survives a child lifetime.
verifiedClean.envelopeAndRefusals: No message smuggles a sixth capability; no control message schema member carries fates, verdicts, D9, Coverage, or frame-type values; refusal families bind structure and surface-local names only, with D9/exit mapping routed to DR-007's successor (whose HARD-BLOCKED standing and blueprint-impact quote reproduce from the register).
verifiedClean.encodingDecision: The canonical-profile avoidance is real: no clause anywhere in the subject requires byte-determinism of control frames - the handshake echoes are value-equality checks, admittedManifestDigest is carried as data computed by admission over manifest bytes, the merged event order records events not frame bytes, and CC-11 makes indifference an obligation. canonical-json-profile.v1 re-measured: CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED with UR-1..UR-5 present, as the subject states.
verifiedClean.ccJoinCoverageExceptB3: J-1 orderings covered by CC-1 (cancel-issued/provider-final-octet both in the event set); J-3 by CC-4 plus CC-1 (EOF per state, death last, bounded-wait expiry observable); J-4 by CC-3 (control side) and CC-1/CC-9 (late provider data after cancel, byte-identity); J-5 by CC-1's teardown-initiated plus CC-4's TEARDOWN-state injections. The no-suppression rule has conformance coverage via CC-1's byte-identity-in-every-ordering plus CC-9's cancellation-mid-stream fixtures.
